claims.text: Al0.3NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr can be produced by mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering.
The as-sintered Al0.3NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr alloy has a single-phase BCC_B2 microstructure.
The sintered alloy should be aged at approximately 800 °C for 10–20 hours under an inert atmosphere.
Aging Al0.3NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr at approximately 800 °C for 10–20 hours will form L12 precipitates.
The aging-induced L12 precipitates will be nanoscale, coherent, and uniformly distributed in the BCC_B2 matrix.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion from the precipitates will increase yield strength and work hardening.
Precipitate coherency minimizes stress concentrations and therefore preserves ductility.
Longer aging can increase precipitate size and reduce precipitate number density.
Aging outside the optimized time or temperature can cause precipitate coarsening or nonuniform distributions in Al0.3NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr.
Precipitate coarsening can embrittle the alloy or otherwise reduce ductility.
Relative to the as-sintered alloy, optimized aging will noticeably increase yield strength.
Relative to the as-sintered alloy, optimized aging will increase work-hardening capability.
Relative to the as-sintered alloy, optimized aging will maintain or slightly improve ductility.
The as-sintered reference alloy lacks significant precipitate formation.
At 800 °C, the equilibrium phase constitution of this alloy is expected to change from the single BCC_B2 state present at the 1200 °C sintering temperature.
The exact optimal aging time and temperature require experimental calibration.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement may vary with precipitate nucleation kinetics and spatial distribution.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement in both yield strength and ductility. Thus an outcome that satisfies the prediction could still be declared falsifying.
